lead: Tesla / TSLA — Musk is back, buy the dip
smaller: Gold and silver / GLD — the fear trade that keeps going
CoreWeave / CRWV — the AI cloud IPO that would not pop
GameStop / GME — the meme stock buys bitcoin
why_lead: Tesla carries the densest retail-attention cluster in the window: a Stocktwits five-day winning streak, TradingView retail-buying headlines, the $2,600 Cathie Wood call repeated across outlets, and national Tesla Takedown protests. Its move is large and two-way (down 10.05% over 20 sessions, up 5.97% over five), which matches a sharp drawdown the crowd is buying. The story the crowd repeats is simple: Musk is back in charge and the dip is the entry.
why_smaller: Gold and silver is the largest non-equity move in the window (gold up 8.36% and silver up 10.97% over 20 sessions), carried by a safe-haven story that is distinct from the Tesla personality trade.
CoreWeave is the AI-infrastructure IPO that priced at $40 and closed flat, a separate AI-bubble narrative with only one close so far.
GameStop is the meme-stock narrative with a bitcoin-treasury hook and the sharpest single-name whipsaw in the attention headlines (a 15% jump, then a 23% slide).
considered_not_chosen: Palantir (PLTR): retail-tagged headlines exist, but the stock is up only 1.10% over 20 sessions, so there is no large move for the attention to match.
Nebius (NBIS): down 31.33% over 20 sessions with Reddit-listicle headlines, but the attention is thin and the next-Nvidia story duplicates the AI basket already covered by CoreWeave.
Oklo and the small-reactor names: heavy attention and steep drawdowns (OKLO down 32.94% over 20 sessions), but the nuclear story is repeated less than the Tesla story; used under underowned themes.
Quantum (QBTS up 38.32% over 20 sessions): the attention is mostly auto-generated Reddit and penny-stock listicles, which is weaker evidence than the Tesla cluster.
Lululemon (down 14.19% in the prior session): a one-day fundamental drop tied to the CEO's inflation comments rather than a crowd narrative; used in the consumer section.
Rheinmetall (up 30.15% over 20 sessions): strong price action, but the evidence is company and analyst headlines rather than retail attention; used in catalysts and underowned themes.
Bitcoin itself: the retail angle is carried by GameStop's treasury pivot and the crypto section; the move on this date is macro risk-off rather than a crowd trade.

Excluded as unusable on this date: a CNBC China factory-activity headline dated March 30 (its content is a report-date-morning release, which falls after the cutoff); a CNBC Hang Seng tech-correction headline dated on a Sunday (doubtful timing); a DW German unemployment headline dated March 28 (release falls on the report date).
